evidence.title: Rijksmuseum NG-MC-674: Model of a Polacre / Daedalus
evidence.read: Full collection text read on 2026-11-14; stated image/plan also inspected where recorded.
confirmed: Museum model has lower/main decks and poop above a panelled cabin, an anchor and capstan.
Catalogue explicitly notes the same ship was variously registered as galliot, ship and schooner.
application: A compact panelled merchant cabin and working cargo hold; supports stating historical type-name uncertainty.
Three-mast polacre rig is not copied: the stock-derived Galeoth keeps its existing two-mast square/lateen arrangement.

notes: Broad cargo hold -0.27L to +0.37L, floor -0.90 m; fitted side casks and planked storage outside the center aisle, with the foremost supported boxes and rope coils in a forward cable/stores zone from +0.15L.
After cabin -0.47L to -0.285L, sole 0.95 m, compact table/bench/berth/locker beneath 1.25 m quarterdeck.
Main 2.2 × 1.6 m cargo hatch +0.08L, small fore stores hatch +0.31L, and offset quarterdeck companion.
Sixteen-gun single battery start moves to -0.24L for bulkhead clearance; no oar benches or rowing gallery are invented.
Galeoth/galliot names cover differing historical rigs and hulls; these are explicit construction analogues, not an identified exact prototype.
The game-derived mixed rig, hull form and count remain decisive.
One offset descending companion enters the cabin through its forward door. No redundant hole is cut through the short cabin roof; this preserves useful furniture and working-deck area.
